Total Marketing Purchase and distribution of 1 November 100 11,304,336
Kenya Limited petroleum products 2010

The primary reason for the acquisition was to complement Total Kenya Limited’s own business activities by providing a more
balanced asset portfolio as well as larger business size to enable it benefit from a growing Kenyan market. The acquisition
increased the number of service stations, strengthened Total Kenya Limited’s position in the airports and provided it with its
own blending plant.
The acquisition was financed by way of;
(a) Capital injection of Kshs 3,900 Million by Total Outer Mer pursuant to the redeemable preference shares issue;
(b) Commercial medium term loans of Kshs 4,680 Million;
(c) Existing short term facilities from Total Kenya Limited’s existing lenders of Kshs 2,724 Million.
(ii) Consideration transferred
The consideration transferred consisted of cash totalling Kshs 11,304,336. Acquisition related costs amounting to Kshs 150
million were included in the consideration transferred as these were costs directly attributed to the business combination.
